input.question: How does an orphaned oil well become a public problem decades after the company that drilled it disappears?

research_context.universe_question: What happens after a mine, dam, cable, factory, or software system is no longer useful to its original owner but remains physically or institutionally present?
research_context.distinct_engine: The environmental and financial afterlife of extraction is more about legal disappearance than physical drilling; plugging costs land on the public.
research_context.evidence_needed: Well registries, corporate histories, state orphan well programs, inspection reports, financial assurance records.
research_context.second_act: The same legal-disappearance mechanism leaves the public holding reclamation costs at abandoned coal mines and orphaned Superfund sites, so the oil-well story opens into a broader afterlife-of-extraction pattern.

value.title: Supplemental Information: Documented Orphan Wells (IOGCC, May 2020)
value.publisher: Interstate Oil and Gas Compact Commission
value.note: IOGCC's own state-survey record of documented orphan wells (2018–2019) by land ownership; 92% on private land, 13% inventory growth year over year. Primary registry/dataset bearing directly on the route's 'well registries' evidence.

value.title: House Memorial 56 — Study of Orphaned Well Ownership Transfer Options (New Mexico, 2026)
value.note: Legislative record defining orphan wells (owner unknown/insolvent/unable to pay), citing $700M–$1.6B state liability and median operator financial assurance of only ~$7,000/well. Primary financial-assurance evidence and explanation of the public-burden mechanism.

value.title: Procedure for Taking Over an Orphan Well
value.note: State regulator's operative definition of an orphan well (inactive 12 months + delinquent operator's P-5 organization report) and financial-assurance conditions for transfer — the legal-disappearance mechanics in the agency's own words.

value.title: Liability for Texas orphan wells soars as numbers, depths, and costs rise sharply
value.publisher: Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis (IEEFA)
value.note: Analysis of RRC data: $202M plugging liability, per-well cost rising $23,807 (2016) to $55,629 (2026), $575M spent on 47,757 wells since 1984. Attributes growth to industry shedding cleanup duties faster than plugging — directly tests the 'plugging costs land on the public' mechanism.

value.title: In Colorado, Amnesty for Oil Producers, Plugging Costs for the State
value.note: Explains the legal-disappearance pathway: a proposed 'voluntary relinquishment' amnesty letting operators forfeit wells to the state and orphan the cleanup onto taxpayers, contrasted with Australia's trailing-liability levy. Answers why public cost arises.

value.title: Utah Modernizes Antiquated Oil And Gas Bonding Rules
value.note: States that bonding rates were a fraction of plugging costs, incentivizing operators to walk away and pass costs to taxpayers; cites a 2019 state performance audit. Regulator-decision/why evidence for financial-assurance shortfall.

value.title: C.S.H.B. 942 Bill Analysis — oil and gas financial security (78th Legislature)
value.note: Legislative committee analysis explaining the purpose of bonding/financial assurance: to give the state a source of funds to plug abandoned wells when the responsible operator cannot or will not. Primary record of why the assurance rule exists.

value.title: H.R. 9029 — Coal Cleanup Taxpayer Protection Act of 2026
value.note: Second-act evidence: bill ending self-bonding and tightening coal-mine reclamation bonds under SMCRA 'to protect taxpayers from liability' — the same legal-disappearance/under-bonding mechanism at abandoned coal mines.

value.title: Abandoned Mine Lands and Superfund: law review on cleanup funding gaps
value.note: Peer-reviewed legal analysis that the single most compelling impediment to abandoned-mine and Superfund cleanup 'is not regulatory but financial,' with no solvent responsible party — extends the orphan-well second act to hardrock mines and CERCLA sites.

value.title: Agency Information Collection: Orphaned Well Site Plugging, Remediation, and Restoration Funding (DOI, 2024)
value.note: Interior's Federal Register notice on state/tribal orphan-well program reporting requirements (Section 40601/BIL). Primary record on a Justia mirror — mark host MIRROR, not the originating publisher.
